correctness.rationale: For alpha>0 and a nonzero finite positive measure compactly supported in a strict positive w-interval, the Fourier transform of (t-iw)^(-1) and critical-density Zak diagonalization give the multiplier (4pi^2/alpha)|F_u(e^{i theta})|^2, where F_u(z)=integral q_w^(1-u)/(1-q_w z)dnu, q_w=exp(-2pi w/alpha). The exact pair kernel K_{q,r}(x)=[1-(q+r)x+qr]/[D_q(x)D_r(x)] is positive for -1<=x<=1, and its partial-fraction decomposition gives a strictly positive x derivative q(1-q^2)/D_q^2 plus its r analogue. Positivity and strict growth of q^(1-u) in u force essential extrema at (u,x)=(0,-1),(1,1), yielding the claimed A and B with their alpha normalization. B^(1/2)/A^(1/2) is a positive probability average of R(R+1)/(R-1), R=e^(2pi w/alpha)>1; this function has its unique global minimum 3+2sqrt(2) at R=1+sqrt(2). Hence B/A>=17+12sqrt(2) and equality requires only the atom at w*=alpha log(1+sqrt(2))/(2pi). Compact support away from zero ensures nonzero finite bounds. Separate Fraction calculations verified pair-kernel algebra/monotonicity on rational grids; these finite checks are not the universal proof.
